title: Leaving Charleston for New York in 1923
summary: He explains that he went north at twelve or thirteen, travelling by train with his uncle's wife to his mother's sister.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, listen Freddie -- how old were you when you left? Did you say?
I came to New York when I was --
I think I was what -- twelve or thirteen or something like that when I came -- to New York.
You left home at twelve or thirteen?
Well, no. My Aunt see -- my mother's sister --
Oh yeah. She had lived in Charleston. Then she moved to New York. But she was in New York, if I can remember, say two or three years or something like that.
And then my mother -- it was just my mother --
Yes. She moved in the Sixties.
Right, right. Do you know where Freddie means Stanley?
Yeah. That was where Benny Carter was.
Right, Benny Carter lived right on 163rd.
Right. That's right. And a whole lot of Irish people lived there.
And um, after that she moved to New York, then I came -- my mother sent me on to New York,
How did she send you up -- on the train?
No, I came with my Aunt -- which is --
She came down to visit or came down to get you?
No, My uncle, who is my mother's brother --
-- left Charleston and went to New York --
-- to my Aunt who was already in New York.
And then I went rode with her on the train.
I see. Well, that's what I wanted to know -- when you went. So really, in a sense, your memories and everything of Charleston -- they're not very full really because they ended at thirteen.
